## Problem

`pyproject.toml` pins `[tool.uv] required-version = "==0.12.7"`. On this operator host the pinned install at `~/.local/share/uv-pins/0.12.7/uv` has been replaced in place by `uv self update` twice (0.13.4 by 2026-10-20, 0.13.6 by 2026-10-28). With any uv other than 0.12.7, `make venv` and `make worktree` stop with "selected uv is version 0.13.6, but this repository requires 0.12.7", so no new worktree can be provisioned. The repository records no defect in uv 0.13.x; the pin exists for reproducibility (CI resolves one uv with no manifest fetch, and local matches CI), not because a later uv is known to break.

Operator decision 2026-10-28: move the pin to 0.13.6.

## Plan

Bump every single-sourced coordinate together, so `scripts/check_uv_pin.py` stays green:

- `pyproject.toml` `required-version` to `==0.13.6`.
- `.github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml`: the 6 `UV_SHA256_*` release checksums for 0.13.6, taken from the astral-sh/uv 0.13.6 release `.sha256` assets.
- `scripts/check_uv_pin.py` `REQUIRED_CHECKSUMS`: the same 6 values.
- `infra/compose/Dockerfile.{mcp,opcert,reviewbot}`: `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.13.6`.
- `docs/local-dev-env.md`, `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md`: version mentions. The CHANGELOG entry for the original pin stays as history.
- `tests/unit/test_uv_pin_guard.py`, `tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py`: pin strings, where they mirror the live pin rather than arbitrary fixtures.
- Check the 0.13.x release notes for changes to `uv sync --locked` and `uv.lock` handling; regenerate nothing unless `uv lock --check` under 0.13.6 fails.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `make venv` and `make worktree` succeed with uv 0.13.6 in a fresh worktree.
- [x] `python scripts/check_uv_pin.py` passes, and every checksum matches the 0.13.6 release asset.
- [x] `uv lock --check` passes under 0.13.6 with the committed `uv.lock`.
- [x] `make verify` shows only the 17 known arm64-host pandoc failures.
- [x] [non-codebase] Gerrit `Verified +1`: every CI job logs uv 0.13.6.
- [x] The MCP image builds with the 0.13.6 uv stage.
